audit: 2026-09-16 scheduled remote agent (seventh fire of the day): one 50 question batch across all four modules, published as eight files data/batches/sched_multi_topic_2026-09-16_g_<module>_N.json. Split 13 Paediatrics, 13 Psychiatry, 12 Obstetrics and Gynaecology and 12 Medicine; tier mix 24 L3, 23 L4 and 3 L5 with no L1 and no L2, taking the bank to 6792 with Paediatrics on 1701, Obstetrics and Gynaecology on 1700, Psychiatry on 1691 and Medicine on 1700. Cell selection: the live matrix before this fire showed Paediatrics, Obstetrics and Medicine on 1688 and Psychiatry on 1678, with L3 deficits against the ideal 50 per cent of 13.09 points in Paediatrics, 12.68 in Obstetrics, 11.80 in Medicine and 11.08 in Psychiatry, L4 deficits against 45 per cent of 13.07, 12.59, 11.77 and 10.61 respectively, and L5 at 5.07 to 5.10 per cent in every module, a deficit of about minus 0.06 points. The strict per question argmax remains degenerate for the fourteenth consecutive fire: run literally it places all 50 questions into Paediatrics and Obstetrics and none into Psychiatry or Medicine, because the Medicine and Psychiatry L3 deficits sit 1.3 and 2.0 points behind the Paediatrics L3 leader and so never enter the 0.5 point near tie window. That allocation would have carried Paediatrics and Obstetrics to 1706 against 1678, a spread of 28, breaching the Section 2 module balance directive that all four modules stay within about 10 of each other, which the routine prompt itself cites as the authority for the tie break. This fire therefore used the same resolution as the previous thirteen: the deficit ranking governs the weighting and the module balance cap bounds the skew, implemented as a greedy per question argmax with a guard refusing any cell whose module total would exceed the lowest module total by more than 10. Within each module the L3 and L4 deficits sit 0.02 to 0.48 points apart, inside the routine's own 0.5 point near tie window, so that tie was resolved by an anti drift rule preferring the cell with fewer questions already allocated in this batch rather than letting a 0.02 point gap award every question to L3; that produced 24 L3 against 23 L4 instead of the 45 against 2 the raw argmax gives. L5 was held at 3 rather than the strict zero the argmax produces, because the standing long term target is to maintain L5 at 5 per cent in each module and an all L3/L4 batch decays that share every fire; the 3 were placed in the three modules with the lowest live L5 share. Final allocation 13/12/13/12 with a spread of 10. Audit: JSON valid, zero em-dashes, zero banned tokens, zero markdown asterisks, no L1 or L2, every stem written from the treating doctor's position, answer length ratio at or below 1.35 in all 50 questions, every source_ref resolving to a label in the question's own sources array, at least two sources per question with an Australian source first, correct answer letters balanced at exactly 10 per letter, tags capped at 3 drawn from the live vocabulary with guideline names confined to sources, explanation summaries 3 to 5 sentences and pearls carrying named drugs, thresholds and timeframes. scripts/dupe_gate.py --new failed on the first run, flagging sched-0916g-med-002 (warfarin reversal for intracranial bleeding, 0.779 against sched-0916f-med-005) and sched-0916g-psych-010 (clozapine myocarditis in week three, 0.790 against sched-0913-psy-002); both were replaced outright with new questions in the same cells, axial spondyloarthritis imaging for Medicine L3 and tic disorder management for Psychiatry L4, and the gate then passed with 0 duplicates against all 6742 existing questions.
